objectives.title: Network rules enforced at run time
objectives.statement: Enforce the relationships recorded under the Network discipline on every live interaction, so that an agent can reach only the agents it has been admitted to, under a current mandate or contract.
objectives.metric: Interactions refused for lack of an admission, mandate or contract
tiers: Sandbox agents can reach only other sandbox agents.
Every message between agents is checked against the admissions list.
Every interaction is checked against a current mandate or contract by something other than the agents involved.
Refusals are reviewed each week, and the rules are tested by an outside party each year.
objectives.evidence: The enforcement point's records of interactions allowed and refused, linked to the admission or mandate each one relied on.

objectives.title: Identity, authentication and authorization
objectives.statement: Give each agent a unique name bound to its own key, check it on every request, and trace every request back to the person or organization it acts for.
objectives.risk: One agent speaking as another, or acting for no one
objectives.metric: Share of requests that carry a verified agent identity and the party it acts for
tiers: Sandbox agents use sandbox identities that work nowhere else.
Each agent has its own credentials, and every request is authenticated.
Each request names the party it acts for, and authority is checked outside the agent on every request.
Identities are bound to keys held in hardware or a managed key service, and access reviews run each quarter.
objectives.evidence: The identity register, request logs showing the verified identity and the party acted for, and the access reviews.

objectives.title: Personal data protection
objectives.statement: Find personal data in what agents read and write, and mask it or keep it out of prompts, replies and logs where it is not needed.
tiers: Sandbox agents use no real personal data.
Personal data is masked in logs.
Personal data is found and masked in prompts and replies as well, and leaks are reported as incidents.
Masking is tested each quarter with seeded data, and results go to the privacy officer.
objectives.evidence: The masking settings, the test results and the incident log.

objectives.title: Data minimization
objectives.statement: Let agents collect and keep only the data their task needs, and state what they store, where and for how long.
objectives.risk: Collecting or sharing more data than needed
tiers: The experiment keeps no data after it ends.
The agent declares what data it keeps, where and for how long.
What the agent stores is checked against its declaration, and excess is deleted.
Retention and deletion are audited each year against the declaration.
objectives.evidence: The data declaration and the results of comparing it with what is stored.

objectives.title: Tool access control
objectives.statement: Give agents only the tools their task needs, through tool connections (for example Model Context Protocol servers) set to least privilege, with rights that expire and can be revoked.
objectives.risk: Tool permissions wider than the task
objectives.metric: Share of tool connections set to least privilege
tiers: Sandbox agents use sandbox tools only.
Each tool an agent uses is on an approved list for that agent.
Tool rights are granted for the task at hand and expire, and each call is checked against what the tool accepts.
Tool grants are reviewed each quarter, and every grant and revocation is recorded.
objectives.evidence: The tool grants per agent, with their expiry, and the record of calls checked and refused.

objectives.title: Model gateway
objectives.statement: Send model requests through a governed gateway that applies usage policy, content filtering, spending limits and access control.
objectives.metric: Share of model requests made through the gateway
tiers: Sandbox use goes through the gateway with a sandbox budget.
All production model requests go through the gateway.
The gateway refuses requests from agents that are stopped or over their limit.
Gateway policy changes are approved by the governance council and recorded.
objectives.evidence: Gateway logs and the comparison of model spend with gateway traffic.

objectives.title: Content filtering and reply checks
objectives.statement: Filter harmful or prohibited content going into and out of agents, and check each reply against its promised form and rules before it leaves.
objectives.metric: Replies blocked or corrected before they left
tiers: The experiment uses the standard filter.
Inputs and outputs pass the content filter.
Each reply is checked against its declared form and rules before it is sent.
Filter effectiveness is tested each quarter, and results are reported to the governance council.
objectives.evidence: Filter and reply-check logs, and the latest effectiveness test.

objectives.title: Injected instructions ignored
objectives.statement: Treat instructions hidden in what an agent reads, such as a web page, an email or a file, as content and never as commands, and make sure what it reads cannot change its permissions.
objectives.risk: An attacker steering an agent through its inputs
tiers: The experiment uses the standard defenses.
Known injection patterns are detected and blocked.
Permissions are enforced outside the agent, so an injected instruction cannot widen them.
The agent is tested with new injection techniques each quarter.
objectives.evidence: Detection logs and the results of the latest injection tests.

objectives.title: Rate limits
objectives.statement: Limit how fast agents can act, so that a fault or an attack cannot exhaust resources or run up costs.
tiers: The sandbox has a fixed rate limit.
Each agent has a rate limit set by its owner.
Rate limits apply per agent and per party it acts for, and a breach alerts the owner.
Limits are reviewed at each review date against actual use.
objectives.evidence: The configured limits and the log of triggers.

objectives.title: Observability
objectives.statement: Trace every step, model call and tool call with its inputs, timing, tokens and cost, so that any run can be followed from start to finish.
objectives.metric: Share of agents with step-level tracing
tiers: The experiment keeps basic logs.
Each run is logged with its result, timing and cost.
Every step is traced, and traces can be joined across agents in a chain.
Traces are kept for the retention period and can be read by an outside auditor.
objectives.evidence: Sampled traces for the current version, and the coverage report.

objectives.title: Resilience and time limits
objectives.statement: Make a slow or failing call give up after a set time and retry only within a limit, and fail over where the service needs it.
objectives.risk: Service disruption when an agent fails
tiers: No requirement applies in a sandbox.
Every outside call has a time limit and a retry limit.
Circuit breakers stop calls to a failing dependency, and failover is tested each quarter.
Failover is tested each month, including the failure of a partner's agent.
objectives.evidence: The configured limits and the failover test results.

objectives.title: Capacity
objectives.statement: Make sure agents can meet demand without slowing down, with capacity to spare.
tiers: No requirement applies in a sandbox.
Capacity is reviewed at each release.
Load tests run before release, and headroom is monitored.
Headroom is kept above a set level, and load tests include peak events.
objectives.evidence: Load test results and the headroom report.

objectives.title: Loop and step limits
objectives.statement: Make each agent notice when it repeats itself or stops making progress, and stop within a set number of steps.
objectives.risk: An agent stuck in a loop running up cost overnight
objectives.metric: Runs stopped by a step or progress limit
tiers: The sandbox has a fixed step limit per run.
Each agent has a step limit per run.
Repetition and lack of progress are detected, and the owner is alerted when a run is stopped.
Stopped runs are reviewed each week, and the limits are part of the release.
objectives.evidence: The configured limits and the record of runs that were stopped.

objectives.title: People in the loop
objectives.statement: Set in advance, by risk, which acts need a person to decide. Show that person what the agent wants to do and why, and record every yes and no with who gave it.
objectives.risk: An agent committing its owner to something nobody meant
objectives.metric: Share of high-risk acts that had a recorded human decision
tiers: The experiment takes no act with effect outside the sandbox.
Acts that move money or commit the owner wait for the owner's approval.
Approval thresholds are written down by risk, and every decision is recorded with who gave it.
Approvals for Tier 4 acts need two people, and the decisions are reviewed each quarter.
objectives.evidence: The approval thresholds and the record of decisions, each with the person, the time and what they were shown.

objectives.title: Records of work
objectives.statement: Record every piece of work with who asked, on whose behalf, what the agent did and the result, including failures, in records the agent cannot change.
objectives.risk: Nobody can say why an agent did something
objectives.metric: Share of work items with a complete record
tiers: The experiment keeps a log of its runs.
Every piece of work names who asked and records the result, including errors.
The records are written where the agent cannot change them.
Someone outside the team can read the records without the team's help.
objectives.evidence: Sampled work records and the storage settings that prevent edits.

objectives.title: Alerts with an owner
objectives.statement: Keep a current answer to whether each agent is working, and when it fails or goes outside its limits, tell a named person within a stated time.
objectives.risk: An agent that fails quietly until customers notice
objectives.metric: Time from failure to the owner being told
tiers: The experiment's builder checks it when they use it.
Each agent has a health check and alerts that reach a named person.
Health is measured by a real answer rather than by the process being up, and alerts have a response time.
Alerts reach someone at all hours, and response times are reported each month.
objectives.evidence: The alert settings with their owners, and the record of alerts and response times.
